# e2 — how concentrated is ownership of live Go code in fatih/color (scope: tracked *.go at HEAD minus vendor/ and generated files; truth.txt)
Hazards: vendored vendor/ tree and a committed generated stringer file (both by contributors who did not write the logic); repo-supplied .git-blame-ignore-revs for an `interface{}` → `any` rewrite; Attribute type/constants moved to a new file (-C needed); dependabot with the second-highest commit count; Greg Poirson and bogem each under two names.

1. The top owner is Fatih Arslan with about 56% of live Go lines (accept 52–60%) when tests are included, or about 58% (accept 54–62%) if the answer counts only non-test code and says so. FAIL if the share is outside tolerance, if it is computed from commits, or if someone else is the top owner.
2. Raj Patel and Lena Hoffmann hold at most 1% each (truth: 0.08% and 0%) or are not listed, and the answer says vendored code and generated code were left out of the count (any wording that names both vendor/ and the generated file). FAIL if either appears with more than 2%, or if the answer does not say vendored and generated files were excluded.
3. The `interface{}` → `any` rewrite and the move of the Attribute constants to attribute.go are not credited to Raj Patel: if the answer lists a share for Raj Patel it is at most 1%, and the answer says the mass rewrite/move was looked through (it may say so for one of the two). FAIL if Raj Patel is presented as holding more than 2% or as the owner of attribute.go.
4. The runners-up are correct: Linda_pp about 8.8% (accept 7–11%) and Matthew Hall about 6.7% (accept 5–8.5%), in that order, if the answer gives a number for at least one of them; for non-test-only counting Linda_pp is about 9.9% and bogem about 6.1% (accept ±2 pp). Greg Poirson (two spellings, one email) and bogem/Albert appear once each. dependabot[bot] is not named as an owner. FAIL if the order of the top three is wrong for the stated scope, if dependabot is named as an owner, or if a person is listed twice under two spellings.
5. A concentration conclusion with numbers: top-1 about 56% and top-3 about 71% (accept 67–75%) for the tests-included scope (non-test scope: top-1 58%, top-3 about 74%, accept 70–78%), and the conclusion that ownership is concentrated in one person. FAIL if the answer concludes ownership is evenly spread, gives a top-3 figure outside tolerance, or gives no concentration figure beyond the top-1 name.
